en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Spell for Exorcising Possession. At that time, the Buddha was in the kingdom of Śrāvastī at the [Miao-long]... [omitted].
He addressed all sentient beings: "The sins one commits cannot be fully recounted; [only] the Way can cause them to be opened."
"Wu, I shall now explain for you the views concerning the past and the future.

'In the past, during the time of the Buddha Śūnyarāja, there was an old man in the Anāthapiṇḍada Garden who, before a fox’s den, burned fat as a lamp. At midnight, the sun, moon, and five planets descended to create malevolent charms and sorcery; they drew upward upon the celestial deities and downward upon the Five Emperors. They further drew upon the mountain spirits and the General of the River Lord, and again drew upon the great deities of the five paths, summoning a hundred ghosts to create malevolent charms and sorcery.'"

Some act as reed-makers; some fashion human effigies; some compose talismans, perform suppressive rites, or cast curses; some take the surnames and names of others; some take thorns; some take yellow earth; or they speak alone toward the sun or moon, unaware of their own actions.

They may take someone’s clothes, or their sashes, or five-colored threads; they may take someone’s steamer-cord, or their jars, pots, or earthenware vessels; they may take the hair of someone’s donkeys, horses, oxen, sheep, pigs, or dogs; or they may take someone’s tools for the five crafts, or door-wedges, or spoons and chopsticks to create malevolent spirits or *gū*-poisons.

They may use *qímá* or *zōumǎ* fibers, or pierce a person’s body, or pierce a person’s heart or fetus; they may calculate a person’s hands and feet, or needle the eye sockets, or needle the waist and back.

Some take human head-hair; some take yellow earth; some take five-colored silks; some take the upper or lower garments and sashes of people; some bewitch the field crops of others; or they seize a group of people, lift them up toward a wall, and speak to them alone.

Some create images in the form of beasts, or images with human heads; some produce talismans, incantations, or curses for malevolent spirits; or they cause people to speak in human voices that are contrary to reason.

They may possess the human households' oxen, horses, sheep, dogs, chickens, pigs, or dogs; they may cause disputes among living people; or they may take the form of a horse, the form of a ghost or spirit, or the forms of an ox, a sheep, a pig, or a dog.
“The person who practices sorcery has no path in life or death, yet they forcibly kill the virtuous and good.

If one teaches another to do so, there will be a thousand calamities and ten thousand sins; the creator shall personally bear the three beams and six pillars [of retribution]. These ten thousand sins and calamities will return to afflict the original master and cause their own destruction. Depart immediately for three thousand six hundred and ten *li*; you must not linger for long.”

Now I invite the Divine King of the Blue Emperor of the East to come and eat the belly of the person possessed by demons; now I invite the Divine King of the White Emperor of the West to come and eat the head of the person possessed by demons; now I invite the Divine King of the Red Emperor of the South to come and eat the eyes of the person possessed by demons; now I invite the Divine King of the Black Emperor of the North to come and eat the feet of the person possessed by demons; now I invite the Divine King of the Yellow Emperor of the Center to come and eat the hands of the person possessed by demons.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva in the assembly named Mahābala. He adjusted his robes, prostrated before the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Your disciple does not understand the nature of sin and merit. Observing the sentient beings of this world, I see that many commit the five heinous crimes and do not believe in the Primordial Way; they prey upon one another with constant malevolence. They do not know that by so doing they will be born in heaven to receive joy, nor do they know that there is hell with its sorrows and sufferings; instead, they torment and consume one another through sorcery and malevolent charms against the virtuous.
"We only pray that the World-Honored One will, for the sake of his disciples, provide a detailed explanation so that they may attain the traces of the Path and deliver all beings.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta:
"You have not yet understood; I shall now explain it in detail for you all. Listen attentively."

I have dispatched the Four Heavenly Kings and their retinues to descend into the world to cure all manner of evils; they shall not rest until they have done so. Depart quickly for a thousand li, and you may escape.

The mantra says: The male spirit-demon is named Ban Yongdu; the female spirit-demon is named Ban Shi Nu. Now I know your clan name and your personal name. If you act as a malevolent spirit or a sorcerer, you shall instead suffer the calamity thereof.
"You have taught others to act while you yourself have met with ruin.

I now summon the Four Heavenly Kings to record the names of those possessed by demons; I shall now cast a spell so that the heads of these possessed ones shall shatter into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
Know now your name and surname: depart quickly for another region; you must not remain here."
"I shall now invoke the Buddha to come; may the head of the person possessed by the spell be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
I shall now invoke the Four Heavenly Dragon Kings to come; may the head of the person possessed by the spell be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree."
"Now we shall summon Ābāng to come; he shall cast a spell so that the person's head is split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree, and may not remain as it is.
The Buddha possesses such a great divine mantra; by this, the head of the possessing spirit shall be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree."
"Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra to come; may the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Mahāprajña to come; may the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree."
"I now invoke the Bodhisattva Further Illumination to come; may the head of the person bewitched by spells be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
I now invoke the Bodhisattva Moonlight to come; may the head of the person bewitched by spells be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree."
"Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Mengguang to come; by his incantation, the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit shall break into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Huoguang to come; by his incantation, the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit shall break into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree."
"Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Puṣpārāma to come; may the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Candraprabha to come; may the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree."
"Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Wenguang (Text-Light) to come; he shall shatter the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Longguang (Dragon-Light) to come; he shall shatter the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree."
"Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Starlight to come; he shall curse the person possessed by a malevolent spirit, causing their head to split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.

Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Thousand Suns to come; he shall curse the person possessed by a malevolent spirit, causing their head to split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree."

"Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Samantaprabha to come; by his incantation, may the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit shatter into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Mahāprabha to come; by his incantation, may the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit shatter into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree."
"Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Tongguang (Equal Light) to come; may the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
Now I shall invite the Bodhisattva Rizhong (Midday) to come; may the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree."
"I now invoke the Bodhisattva Jianli (Establishment) to come; may the head of the person possessed by the spell be shattered into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
I now invoke the Bodhisattva Shuwang (Tree King) to come; may the head of the person possessed by the spell be shattered into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree."

"Now I shall invoke the Dragon-Heaven Bodhisattva to come; by this incantation, the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit shall be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.

Now I shall invoke the Earth-Trembling Bodhisattva to come; by this incantation, the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit shall be split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree."
"Now I shall invite the Divine King of the Blue Emperor of the East to come; he who casts spells and possesses people must not remain.
Now I shall invite the Divine King of the Red Emperor of the South to come; he who casts spells and possesses people must not remain."
Now I shall invite the White Emperor King of the Western Quarter to come; he must not allow those bewitched by incantations to remain.
Now I shall invite the Black Emperor King of the Northern Quarter to come; he must not allow those bewitched by incantations to remain.

Now I shall summon the sun, the moon, the five planets, and the twenty-eight lunar mansions to come; they shall seize the person possessed by a malevolent spirit so that they cannot remain, and must depart in haste for a thousand li.

"From the east, the Great Deer shall come to devour the body of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit; from the south, the centipede shall come to devour the eyes of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit; from the west, the white elephant shall come to devour the head of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit; from the north, the black elephant shall come to peck at the heart-organ of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit; and from the center, the Divine Dragon King of the Yellow Emperor shall come to devour the spirit of the person possessed by a malevolent spirit."

"I have seen those possessed by demons with their eyes wide open and corners drawn back; some act wildly, no longer resembling human form; they may be at people's gates, or inside houses, or atop mortars and grinding stones, or leaping incessantly across people's fields."

Whether on the first day of the first month, the New Year’s day, the fifteenth day of the first month, or on seasonal festivals, they may burn fat as fuel for lamps and recite incantations without ceasing, saying:
"I know your name; you must not remain here, depart quickly to another region!"
Whether sitting they shall perish, or standing they shall be extinguished; their heads shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.
Should red-mouthed or red-tongued spirits arise, the Bodhisattva’s incantation shall cause them to be extinguished; depart quickly and do not linger long.
At that time, the World-Honored One said:
"I now announce to all sentient beings of the ten directions: for the sake of you all—sons and daughters of good family—I shall now speak this Sūtra of the Spell against Demons."

At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions, the seven Buddhas of the past, the sixteen princes-Buddhas, the bodhisattvas of the heavens, devas and humans, arhats, the four great kings, the eight classes of devas and nāgas, various benevolent spirits, and those who have attained the four fruits of the path, all assembled together at the summit of Mount Sumeru beneath the Dragon-Flower Tree. They deliberated together on how sentient beings might be delivered.

If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, men, or women who can burn incense and pay homage to the Buddha, and who receive, uphold, and make offerings to this sutra without ceasing, they shall cause people to obtain merit.
If those who suffer from grief and pain can give rise to wholesome thoughts, they shall all obtain the bliss of heaven.
If there are those who recite this sutra, they should first purify their bodies, practice the Way, burn incense, and uphold it; thus they may attain liberation.
If one can recite this sutra seven times, the head of the possessing spirit will split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree, and all sufferings shall be completely liberated.

At that time, all sentient beings in the assembly, having heard the sutra, were filled with joy and reverence; they prostrated before the Buddha, took up its recitation, and practiced it accordingly. *The Sutra of the Charm Against Possession*.
